property_summary: The return value of `getAssertionPolicy` should always have `blockAssertion` set to `false`.
Calling assertionDisputedCallback on any assertionId should not revert.
For any bytes32 assertionId, calling assertionDisputedCallback does not change the result of getAssertionPolicy.
The return value of getAssertionPolicy has arbitrateViaEscalationManager equal to false for any input assertionId.
Calling assertionDisputedCallback on an assertionId does not change the return value of getAssertionPolicy for that assertionId.
Calling assertionDisputedCallback with any bytes32 assertionId should not change the arbitrateViaEscalationManager field returned by getAssertionPolicy(false).
Calling assertionDisputedCallback with any bytes32 assertionId does not change the return value of getAssertionPolicy (the returned struct's fields remain unchanged).
getAssertionPolicy always returns discardOracle as false
getAssertionPolicy always returns discardOracle as false
The assertionDisputedCallback function does not revert when called with any bytes32 assertionId.
A call to assertionDisputedCallback never changes the value returned by a subsequent call to getAssertionPolicy for the same assertionId.
The discardOracle field in getAssertionPolicy return value is always false.
After calling assertionDisputedCallback, the validateDisputers field of the AssertionPolicy returned by getAssertionPolicy for any assertion ID must be false.
The function assertionDisputedCallback does not revert when called by any address.
After calling assertionDisputedCallback(bytes32), msg.sender is not checked, so the rule is that the call does not revert regardless of who calls it (i.e., it always succeeds).
Calling assertionDisputedCallback with any bytes32 assertionId does not revert even when called by a non-optimisticAsserter address, due to the removed onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier check.
